sentences.text:
Mr.Vikas A. Tiwari, Advocate for Respondent no.2.
 Mrs.M.M.Deshmukh, Additional P.P for State.
 Api Suryawanshi, Manpada Police Station, present.

Coram : Prakash D. Naik And
 K.C.Sant, Jj.

Date : 16th February 2024
 Pc :
1. Leave to amend cause title.
Petitioner is permitted to mask  name of Respondent no.2.

Amendment be carried out forthwith.
 2. Petitioner is chargesheeted for offences under Sections 376(1)
376(2)(n), 354, 354(A)(D), 352, 452, 342, 504, 506, 509, 323 of  Indian Penal Code.
3. The FIR was registered at the instance of Respondent no.2 vide  CR No.I-372 of 2018 on 16th July 2018 with Manpada Police Station.
Respondent no.2 has alleged that she got acquainted with accused in  2006.
They were in love.
She informed about it to her parents.
There was objection of her parents.
In 2012 she performed marriage  with another person.
She again got in touch with Petitioner in 2015.
The Applicant visited her house.
She was subjected to sexual assault.

sentences.text: She was threatened.
Under the threats there was repeated acts of  sexual assaults.
In April-2018 the Petitioner threatened the  complainant that he would disclose about their relationship to her  husband.
The FIR was registered thereafter on 16th April 2018.
4. Learned advocate for Petitioner submitted that parties have  resolved their differences.
The relationship was consensual.
From  the tenor of FIR it appears that complaint was lodged after the  husband came to know about the relationship between Petitioner  and complainant.
The complainant has no objection for quashing  the FIR.
5. Learned APP submitted that the FIR refers to the nature of  relationship between Petitioner and Respondent no.2.
The  complainant has referred to the threats issued by Petitioner.
6. Learned advocate for Respondent no.2 submitted that  Respondent no.2/complainant has no objection for quashing the FIR  and charge sheet.
Respondent no.2 has filed the affidavit.
The  affidavit is taken on record.

The affidavit mentions that Respondent  no.2 and Petitioner have amicably settled the matter and Respondent  no.2 has no grievance against Petitioner and no objection to quash  the FIR filed against Petitioner.
7. Respondent no.2 is present in the Court through Video  Conference.
She has expressed her no objection to quash the  proceedings.
She has admitted the contents of affidavit.
The  affidavit is taken on record.
8. On perusal of the FIR and charge sheet it appears that  Petitioner and Respondent no.2 were known to each other.
They  were in relationship.
